sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Manish Joshi,Rakesh Kumar Verma Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kartikey Singh,Sameer Khan Hon'ble Neeraj Tiwari,J.
Supplementary affidavit and short counter affidavit filed today, are taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for State and Sri Jainendra Sharma, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2.

The present application under section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing the entire proceedings bearing charge sheet No. 127 of 2018 in Case No.963 of 2018 (State Vs. Shameem @ Waseem and others) arising out of Case Crime No.110 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 323, 328, 325, 504, 307 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Dilari, District Moradabad pending in the Court of A.C.J.M., Court Shameem Alias Waseem And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165741892/
1 No. 5, Moradabad.
Learned counsel for the applicants has filed supplementary affidavit and submitted that present matter is arising out of matrimonial dispute and both the parties have entered into compromise and the said compromise has been filed before C.J.M., Moradabad on 9.10.2019.

sentences.text: Copy of the said compromise has been annexed as Annexure-SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit.

Learned counsel for the applicants states that the matter has been compromised and the opposite party no. 2 does not want to pursue the matter any further as the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, therefore, the present case may be finally decided.

Sri Jainendra Sharma, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 has filed short counter affidavit and submitted that the disputes have been amicably settled between the parties, therefore on the basis of compromise the Hon'ble Court may kindly be quash the entire proceeding of the aforesaid case.
In view of above, the applicants and opposite party no. 2 do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them.
The matter has been mutually settled between the parties, therefore, no useful purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter further.

Thus in view of the well settled principle of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi) Vs. State of Haryana) as well as the judgement of the Apex Court reported in J.T. 2008 SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Burea of Investigation and another) as well as Judgment of the Apex Court reported in (2012)10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab)
and reported in 2014 Supreme Today 642 (Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab and another), the proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.
